assertions.name: trefoil_and_nucleon_are_not_psd_feasible
assertions.source: trefoil [('sigma_1^3 (B_2 form)', False), ('(s1 s2)^2 (B_3 form)', False), ('(s1 s2)^3 (full twist)', True)]; nucleons [('proton', '1/3'), ('neutron', '1/3')]

assertions.name: determined_K_is_not_psd_feasible
assertions.source: 2H: K PSD in 1/11; 3H: K PSD in 2/30; 3He: K PSD in 2/30

description: EXPLORATORY (bean t7qv): takes the owner's steer that K should be an SDP solution via knot convolution, and follows it to the end. (1) The convolution K = rho(atom).rho(free)^-1 DETERMINES K from the canonical substrate word — no free variable, so nothing to optimise. (2) Its derived closure arity is c(K) = 2A+1 (46/46 exact); no registry binding_link_name has it (Hopf 2 vs 5, 8_11 1 vs 7, L6a4 3 vs 7). (3) PSD-feasibility in the seminormal rep is a PARITY condition — rho(sigma) has eigenvalues {q0, -1/q0}, so sigma^k is PSD iff k is even — which passes the unknot and every full twist and cannot select. (4) It rejects the trefoil (-0.731) that binding_k_solver.py names as the unique PSD-feasible constituent, and both nucleon words. (5) The determined K is PSD in 1/11, 2/30, 2/30 blocks, every survivor being 1-DIMENSIONAL — no block of dim >= 2 survives for either object at any A. So K is infeasible for the program said to select it. Machinery validated 4/4 against binding-link-psd-feasibility-probe. No fit; no objective proposed; no knot proposed.
caveats: Wedderburn evaluation is at f64, as in binding_k_solver.py. The eigenvalue magnitudes are O(1) and every conclusion is a SIGN conclusion, so f64 is adequate; declared, not laundered.

PSD is tested on the symmetric part, i.e. on the quadratic form x'Mx — rho_lambda(K) is not symmetric in general. The validation run reproduces all four recorded H_3 results under this convention, including locating 6_2's failure in the standard (2,1) block; the magnitude there is -0.8334 here against -0.89 recorded, a q-pin/normalisation difference. The argument uses the sign and the block, which agree.

include_inter=False is taken as the constituent product: the generator layout is identical to the full word minus the inter-nucleon crossings, which is what the factorisation T_w(atom) = K . (x)_i T_w(nucleon_i) means. binding_k_solver.py builds K from the HISTORICAL knot braid words instead; this probe uses the canonical substrate word, which is the point.
